The current Title II implementation doesn't forbid this practice; it only addresses paid prioritization of traffic (accepting money from a third party to prioritize their traffic). I do think a measure of net neutrality is needed in order to prevent ISPs who offer other services from prioritizing their own services, but that's exactly the loophole in Title II that Verizon is exploiting here.

I'd rather see a Title II implementation that says ISPs can prioritize traffic as required for network management (currently included in Title II) BUT cannot accept payment for prioritization AND cannot affect the speed of traffic for the services they provide or services that directly compete with the services they provide.

Right now we have a situation that's kind of like a bus company owning both buses and the road itself. They've got no reason to let other traffic (taxis or private cars) use the roads evenly, so they're going to do everything they're allowed to do to promote their bus service and make it the most compelling option.
